title: Sum in parallel, read after join

blocks.text: Two of the page's six rules carry values between threads without any lock or `volatile`: **thread start** (everything before `t.start()` is visible inside `t`) and **thread join** (everything `t` did is visible once `t.join()` returns). The page's `ThreadStartHappensBefore` and `CorrectOrdering` examples lean on exactly these.

Write `ParallelSum.sum(List<LongSupplier> parts)`. It starts **one new thread per part**; each thread calls its part and stores the result in a plain `long[]` slot of its own (no `volatile`, no lock, no atomic). The method then returns the total of all the slots. The start and join rules are what make the slots safe to read, so read them only when they are guaranteed visible.

items: every part runs on a thread you started for it, never on the calling thread;
a part may take a long time: the total must still include it.

cases.says: It adds up what every part computes, each part run on a thread of its own.
Each part runs on a thread started for it, never on the caller's thread.
The sum is read only after join() returns for every worker, so no slow part is ever missed, wherever it stands in the list.

concepts: Writes made before Thread.start() are visible in the started thread, and a thread's writes are visible once join() on it returns.
